message.content:
<summary>
Turn 1: Agent confirmed /root/druid is a git repo at tag druid-0.20.0 (commit acdc6ee7ea). Attempted to use ripgrep (rg) to search for JavaScript-related code but rg is not installed, so those searches failed.

Turn 2: Switched to grep. Found JavaScript-related query/filter code including processing/src/main/java/org/apache/druid/query/filter/JavaScriptDimFilter.java and processing/src/main/java/org/apache/druid/segment/filter/JavaScriptFilter.java, plus JavaScript aggregators and post-aggregators. No matches for JacksonInject("") via grep (search produced no output).

Turn 3: Grepped for @JacksonInject usages across modules. Identified JavaScriptConfig is injected via @JacksonInject in multiple classes including JavaScriptDimFilter, JavaScriptExtractionFn, JavaScriptAggregatorFactory, JavaScriptPostAggregator, and some indexing/router strategy classes.

Turn 4: Looked for where Jackson InjectableValues are configured. Found mostly test usage; an attempted grep for “addValue(” failed due to an unmatched parenthesis in the grep pattern. Located JavaScriptModule binding (server/src/main/java/org/apache/druid/guice/JavaScriptModule.java binds druid.javascript to JavaScriptConfig). Also collected many JavaScriptConfig references (output clipped).

Turn 5–7: Tried to open GuiceInjectableValues from the wrong module path (server/...) and corrected to core/. Inspected core/src/main/java/org/apache/druid/guice/GuiceInjectableValues.java: it only accepts valueId instances that are Guice Key objects; otherwise it throws an IAE (“Unknown class type … for valueId …”). This suggests injection is not done via string ids.

Turn 8–9: Searched and inspected the custom Jackson annotation introspector: core/src/main/java/org/apache/druid/guice/GuiceAnnotationIntrospector.java. findInjectableValueId returns null if no @JacksonInject; otherwise returns Key.get(genericType) or Key.get(genericType, bindingAnnotation). It does not use any string-based injectable id, implying the exploit’s “empty key” bypass is likely via a different JSON parsing path than standard @JacksonInject id handling.

Turn 10: Inspected processing/src/main/java/org/apache/druid/query/filter/JavaScriptDimFilter.java. Noted it holds JavaScriptConfig injected in constructor and only checks config.isEnabled() inside getPredicateFactory() when actually compiling/using the script (Preconditions.checkState(config.isEnabled(), “JavaScript is disabled”)). This is the intended security gate, but may be bypassed if config can be influenced during deserialization.

Turn 11–12: Located and inspected the sampler endpoint handler indexing-service/.../SamplerResource.java. The POST method consumes JSON and directly accepts a SamplerSpec object (Jersey/Jackson deserialization), then calls sampler.sample(); no explicit request validation occurs here.

Turn 13–14: Located TransformSpec and inspected processing/src/main/java/org/apache/druid/segment/transform/TransformSpec.java. It simply stores a DimFilter “filter” and list of transforms; no JavaScript-specific logic is present in TransformSpec itself.

Turn 15: Attempted to inspect DefaultObjectMapper configuration. Found DefaultObjectMapper is in processing/src/main/java/org/apache/druid/jackson/DefaultObjectMapper.java, but the agent tried to open it from core/ and got “No such file or directory”; DefaultObjectMapper contents were not yet inspected in this window.
</summary>

I found a vulnerability path involving JacksonInject, where it seems that the guice Key based on type can’t be bypassed. However, there's mention of an empty key being used to bypass JS security settings. It makes me wonder about potential injections in JsonConfigurator or annotation introspector.
